hyps.why: Small learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so raising them helps, whereas at high rates raising them destabilizes training.
Very large learning rates diverge, so stepping down rescues training.
Increasing an already large learning rate causes divergence and big accuracy drops.
Shallower networks are more stable at high learning rates, so removing a layer helps there.
With a low, stable learning rate extra depth adds capacity without instability.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which helps when the learning rate is large.
Smaller batches add noise on top of large steps, worsening instability.
Wider layers amplify update magnitudes, making high learning rates more unstable.
Strong L2 causes underfitting, so weakening it from a high value helps while at low values it has no effect.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty worsens underfitting.
